question: How can the GraphRAG literature be organised into a workflow of indexing, retrieval and generation, with its training methods, tasks, benchmarks, industrial systems and open problems?
contributions: A formal definition of GraphRAG and its workflow G-Indexing, G-Retrieval, G-Generation.
Analysis of core technologies and training methods per stage.
Downstream tasks, benchmarks, application domains, metrics, challenges and future directions, plus an inventory of industry GraphRAG systems.

limits: Survey with no experiments of its own; every performance claim is qualitative and unquantified.
Table 1 lists benchmarks and citing methods but no scores, so no method comparison is possible.
Authors concede GraphRAG lacks unified standard benchmarks (Sec 10.6) and that most methods are static and small-scale (Sec 10.1, 10.3).
Text-to-Cypher is touched only briefly (UniOQA, a CQL mention); no systematic coverage of query-language generation.
Dated: covers work up to mid-2024; industrial system list is a snapshot.
Reference list has a duplicated entry (refs 10/11 Freebase, 12/13 SimpleQuestions) and an apparently truncated sentence on Liu et al. [101] in Sec 6.4.2.
practices: Hybrid indexing combining graph, text and vector indices is preferred over one alone (Sec 5.2.4).
Choose retrieval paradigm by balancing accuracy against time complexity: once retrieval for real-time, iterative for accuracy (Sec 6.2.4).
Use fine granularity (nodes, triplets) for simple or latency-critical queries and hybrid granularity for complex ones (Sec 6.3.6).
Use multi-stage retrieval combining cheap non-parametric and costly LM/GNN retrievers (Sec 6.1.4).
Prune/rerank retrieved knowledge (cross-encoder, PageRank, LLM check) and merge duplicates before generation (Sec 6.4.2).
Pick the graph language deliberately: keep it complete, concise and comprehensible (Sec 7.2.1).
Constrain decoding of logical forms to schema items present in the KG to avoid invalid generations (Sec 7.3.2).
Combine query-generated (Cypher) answers with triplet-based answers via a selection mechanism (UniOQA, Sec 7.3.3).
Evaluate both downstream quality and retrieval quality (Sec 9.3.2).
